A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FACTBENCH and VERIFY. Their main text, complete appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original four-model benchmarking results, human annotations of 4,467 units, and analyses of factuality, subjectivity, and refusals.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds three evaluated language models, clustering analysis, and a human audit of 570 undecidable units.

M1.justification: The extraction, decontextualization, retrieval, three-way verification, prompt templates, and hallucination score with alpha = 0.5 are retained. The new tuning explanations and planned updating workflow do not establish a revision to the method used to construct and evaluate the reported benchmark.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 1,000 English FACTBENCH prompts from LMSYS-Chat-1M, covering 150 topics and the same three tiers. WildChat appears only as a proposed future source in v2 Section 10.6.

E2.justification: VERIFY's comparison methods remain FactScore, SAFE, and Factcheck-GPT, with the same adaptations and gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 backbone. The additional leaderboard LMs are response-generating systems being evaluated, rather than new factuality-evaluation baselines.

E3.justification: v2 extends evaluation to three additional LMs and reports hallucination scores alongside factual precision in its leaderboard. Newly reported analyses specify an HDBSCAN grid search and a 100-response, two-annotator audit of 570 undecidable units. The original main benchmarking and 40-prompt human-evaluation designs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial supplementary validation: clustering stability across parameter combinations, a human audit supporting the existing alpha choice, and a difficult-unit comparison with Factcheck-GPT (Sections 10.3, 10.5, and 10.11). Section 7.3 also expands the analysis of unnecessary Gemini refusals. The earlier dependent-unit and subjectivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The retained studies use the same agreement, correlation, and graphical uncertainty reporting. The new audit's 85.5% annotator agreement is another result using an existing reporting practice; no new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, but v2 Table 3 adds Claude-3.5-Sonnet, CommandR+, Mistral-Large-2, and hallucination scores. Its expanded Easy-tier ranking places Mistral-Large-2 at 92.00 factual precision versus GPT4-o at 91.63. Table 2 adds the 57% factual versus 43% non-factual audit finding, and Section 7.3 adds refusal breakdowns. v1 Table 3's detailed label and unit statistics are removed.

T1.justification: The hallucination-score and factual-precision equations retain their mathematical content. v2's usefulness-score formula formalizes the aggregation already described in v1. Neither version contains substantive theoretical proofs or theorems.

C1.justification: Both claim an updatable, diverse FACTBENCH benchmark, verifiability-aware three-way evaluation through VERIFY, and stronger agreement with human judgments. The principal findings about the original four LMs, subjectivity, and Gemini refusals remain. Additional appendix evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 9 explicitly discusses single-model evaluation bias and the costs and design challenges of using multiple evaluators. It expands the existing recall limitation with open-ended examples. v2 also elaborates conservative refusal behavior and removes v1's suggestion that consistent model rankings imply evaluator reliability.

D1.justification: Sections 10.3–10.6 newly disclose HDBSCAN settings, the parameter grid, default settings for other clustering stages, explicit usefulness aggregation, and planned annual updating operations. These improve documentation without demonstrating changed settings for the existing benchmark. The project link and operational prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds WildChat (Zhao et al., 2024) as a potential future source of user interactions. The principal cited works and positioning against FactScore, SAFE, VeriScore, and Factcheck-GPT otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens several passages, shortens the conclusion, renames Section 3, and reorganizes the expanded appendix. A dedicated Limitations section replaces the earlier acknowledgement, ethics, and reproducibility sections. Most of the main narrative and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from one column to two, with resized and relocated figures, tables, captions, and prompt blocks. Existing plots retain their content despite renumbering. New audit and leaderboard tables are added, while v1's detailed label-statistics table is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 adds empirical support for the retained alpha choice, supplies previously unreported clustering settings, and clarifies substantive limitations. These improve the design's justification and reproducibility, while the expanded leaderboard increases benchmark usefulness. Removing v1 Table 3 loses detailed statistics, but the added evidence and documentation provide a modest net improvement to an otherwise stable main study.
